summary: Today’s pulse tracks Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas, NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain, and Anthropic shares fall after blockbuster opening as wider tech sell-off continues. Across BBC, Ars Technica, and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are dimon, increase, and unfair. In the background, Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too and Gérard Depardieu and French author investigated over sexual allegations keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas
headlines.description: The US president provided little detail on the potential policy, saying others in his team were hearing about it for the first time.

headlines.title: NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain
headlines.description: "We tend to have a lot of technical discussion and debate. That point will continue to be debated."

headlines.title: Anthropic shares fall after blockbuster opening as wider tech sell-off continues
headlines.description: Other tech companies have also taken a hit as share markets broadly slump.

headlines.title: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.
headlines.description: CTIA said jamming test showed "interference... up to two and a half miles away."

headlines.title: Gérard Depardieu and French author investigated over sexual allegations
headlines.description: A judicial investigation was launched after a complaint was filed last year over "allegations of a sexual nature".

headlines.title: JP Morgan boss says he will find ways to offset ‘unfair’ rise in UK tax on banks
headlines.description: Jamie Dimon says he is ‘setting an example’ in seeking to claw back Labour’s increase in surcharge, from 3% to 6% Jamie Dimon, the chief executive of JP Morgan, has said he will find ways to offset the chancellor’s tax rise for banks, calling the increase unfair. Speaking at an event in London on Thursday, Dimon said he would seek to claw back the increase and was “setting an example so that [governments] understand the trade-offs of these unfair penalties”.

headlinePool.description: Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering in February.

headlinePool.description: Modeling predicts plume of neurotoxic lead could reach up to 100 miles away.

headlinePool.title: Home Alone sequel reportedly in development with Macaulay Culkin returning
headlinePool.description: Christmas comedy hit is set for a follow-up from the point of view of the father with Seth Rogen as writer and producer A Home Alone sequel is reportedly in development with original star Macaulay Culkin set to return. According to Puck’s Matthew Belloni , Culkin met with Disney executives earlier this year with a pitch for a follow-up and now the project has been met with a green light. The new Home Alone film will bring the 46-year-old back to the franchise as Kevin McCallister for a comedy that, according to Deadline , will be from the father’s point of view.

headlinePool.title: White House removes cyber-security chief after series of tech outages
headlinePool.description: He has been fired after losing the confidence of new White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, according to reports.

headlinePool.title: Police arrest teacher who missed sentencing after indecent assault conviction
headlinePool.description: Sally-Anne Bowen was found guilty of having sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the 1980s A chemistry teacher who had sexual relationships with two pupils at a boys’ school in the late 1980s has been arrested by police in Hampshire after she failed to turn up to her sentencing hearing. Sally-Anne Bowen, 65, could not be found at her home by Metropolitan police officers on Friday morning after a warrant was issued for her arrest, a court heard.

headlinePool.title: ‘Worth fighting for’: senators vow to restore financial watchdog agency after Guardian investigation
headlinePool.description: Democrats – including incoming banking chair and both majority leader candidates – said wealthy interests were prioritized over the needs of working Americans In response to a Guardian investigation , four US Senate Democrats say they will work to resurrect a financial watchdog agency that has abandoned dozens of enforcement actions under the second Trump administration . The Guardian found that after the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) dropped more than 20 lawsuits against banks and corporations accused of a range of financial misconduct, complaints against those firms rose by an average of more than 75%. In many of these recent complaints, consumers described the same issues the CFPB’s suits had sought to address.

headlinePool.title: Lauren Boebert says Trump ‘did some things to hurt’ her constituents
headlinePool.description: Controversial Colorado Republican narrowly lost House seat in midterms but says ‘I’m not mad at the president’ Lauren Boebert says Donald Trump “did some things that hurt” her constituents before they voted the pugnacious Colorado Republican out of her US House seat during midterm elections, which saw her and the president’s party lose control of Congress. “This could be a referendum on President Trump,” Boebert said to the Associated Press in an interview published on Friday. “It could be the referendum on Congress or the Republican party. I think it’s all of it.

headlinePool.title: Florida mechanic found guilty of murdering British woman who attorney says came to US to die
headlinePool.description: Dwain Hall was convicted of stabbing Sonia Exelby, a music teacher who prosecutors say suffered from mental illness A Florida mechanic has been found guilty of stabbing to death a British music teacher, whom he convinced to travel to the United States. Dwain Hall, an auto repair and tow truck driver, groomed 32-year-old Sonia Exelby from Portsmouth, England, on a fetish website before luring her to the US.

headlinePool.title: Spain frees wealthy US-sought activist on bail as Irish police raid Dublin home
headlinePool.description: Pro-Palestinian donor James ‘Fergie’ Chambers released as court considers extradition request In a blur of events surrounding the Trump administration’s effort to extradite James “Fergie” Chambers, Spain released the wealthy US activist and donor on bail even as Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner, Stella Schnabel, acting on a request from US authorities. Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.
